title: An Integrated Deep Learning and Molecular Dynamics Simulation-Based Screening Pipeline Identifies Inhibitors of a New Cancer Drug Target TIPE2.
summary: A hybrid deep-learning, docking and molecular-dynamics screen nominated TIPE2 ligands. Biolayer interferometry tested four: UM-164 bound at Kd 4.97 μM, while three alternatives showed much weaker reported binding. A PIP2 competition assay does not establish cancer-treatment efficacy.
ai_technology: DFCNN dense fully connected neural network
organization: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology

evidence.tested: BLI tested four selected compounds: UM-164 Kd 4.97 μM, golvatinib about 189 μM and fedratinib about 298 μM. FIIN-3 was described as lacking reactivity; the discussion’s approximately 0.858 M fit is not evidence of appreciable binding. A separate UM-164 competition assay reduced TIPE2–PIP2 binding.
evidence.unknown: The assays establish biochemical binding and in-vitro competition only, not cellular target engagement or treatment efficacy. The paper's conclusion calls UM-164 low-nanomolar, but the reported BLI Kd is 4.97 μM.
evidence.ai_role: DFCNN and DeepBindBC binding predictors, docking and molecular-dynamics simulations prioritized compounds for experimental TIPE2 binding and PIP2-competition assays.

source_review.scope: Frontiers primary Methods on DFCNN/DeepBindBC and Results/Discussion on BLI binding, competition, and internal affinity inconsistencies.
